reading.title: Supporting Black-Owned Businesses
reading.passage:
In today's economy, supporting Black-owned businesses has become an important topic of discussion. Venture capital, which is funding provided by investors to startup companies, is often highlighted as a key resource. However, studies show that Black entrepreneurs receive a disproportionately small share of venture capital funding compared to their peers.

Bank finance, rather than venture capital, serves as the real driver for a business to grow from small to medium, and medium to big. For the vast majority of entrepreneurs, access to fair lending from banks is far more impactful than the rare chance of securing venture capital. Improving access to bank finance is therefore the most meaningful way to support Black entrepreneurs in scaling their businesses.

The challenge goes beyond funding. Black business owners sometimes face cultural misunderstandings during presentations. For instance, a well-meaning white entrepreneur once offended a predominantly Black audience by making frivolous assumptions about their community. This illustrates the importance of relevance and sincerity in cross-cultural business communication.

Many organizations have recognized these barriers and are working to create more inclusive entrepreneurship ecosystems. Programs that provide mentorship, networking opportunities, and leadership training aim to level the playing field. How can talented, highly motivated Black entrepreneurs achieve their full potential? The answer lies in systemic change — improving access to capital, education, and markets for all.

reading.title: Earth's Major Systems and Spheres
reading.passage:
What is the most important part of our environment? Is it the land we walk on, the air we breathe, or the water we drink? It turns out that no single feature is more significant than the others are. The environment is made up of interactive systems, each as crucial as the next. There are five main systems, or spheres, on Earth: the geosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, and biosphere.

The first system, the geosphere, consists of the interior and surface of Earth, both of which are made up of rocks. It includes everything from the thin layer of soil on the surface to the enormous, dense core at the center of the planet. The movement of tectonic plates, volcanic eruptions, and the formation of mountains are all processes within the geosphere.

The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding Earth. It protects life by absorbing ultraviolet radiation and regulating temperature. The hydrosphere is composed of all the liquid water on Earth — the oceans, rivers, and lakes that sustain life.

The cryosphere contains all the frozen water on Earth, including glaciers, ice caps, and permafrost. Finally, the biosphere, a global ecosystem that encompasses all the living things on Earth, is the fifth system. Each of these five enormous and complex systems interact with one another. Because these systems are interconnected, what affects one can affect another. Scientists study these interactions to understand how changes in one sphere can have cascading effects across the entire planet.

reading.title: Globalization and International Trade
reading.passage:
Globalization is a process of interaction and integration among people, companies, and governments worldwide. As transportation and communication technologies have improved, the world has become increasingly connected. The experiences of people around the world have become more similar as a result.

Some view globalization as a form of "Americanization," or the exporting of American culture and values to other countries. However, globalization is not a one-way street; cultures influence each other in complex ways. Globalization was accelerated in the nineteenth century with the Industrial Revolution, as improved machinery and transportation allowed goods and ideas to cross borders more easily than ever before.

To increase trade, many countries have created free trade agreements with other countries. The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which went into effect in 1994, is a well-known example. NAFTA eventually ended all tariffs on trade goods between the United States, Mexico, and Canada. Most large corporations now operate in many countries around the world.

The globalization of the economy has also led to the spread of international law. In 2002, the International Criminal Court was established to prosecute individuals for crimes against humanity. Some people argue that globalization has led to economic inequality between nations, while others contend that it has lifted millions out of poverty. Food patterns, cultural traditions, and even languages have been affected by the increasing interconnectedness of nations.

Despite its benefits, globalization remains controversial. Critics point to outsourcing of jobs, environmental concerns, and the loss of local cultural identity as negative consequences. The continued growth of globalization in the twenty-first century will depend on how nations balance economic opportunity with social responsibility.

reading.title: Graphene for Solar Cells
reading.passage:
Laws of physics limit the maximum efficiency of traditional silicon solar cells to around 29 percent. To surpass this limit, scientists have turned to tandem solar cells that combine silicon with newer materials such as perovskites. These tandem cells can theoretically achieve efficiencies above 30 percent by capturing a broader range of the solar spectrum.

However, integrating perovskite layers with silicon efficiently has proven challenging. The interface between the two materials must allow charges to flow smoothly, or energy is lost. Researchers began to dig into the possibilities of using graphene — a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb pattern — as an interface material.

Scientists from the Graphene Flagship initiative, including Aldo di Carlo from the University of Rome Tor Vergata, demonstrated that graphene-based interface layers dramatically improve the performance of tandem cells. Their research, published in the journal Joule, showed tandem cells with graphene achieving record-breaking efficiency, paving the way towards breaking the 30 percent barrier and significantly reducing the Levelized Cost of Energy.

The Graphene Flagship's Spearhead Project GRAPES has set up a pilot production line for graphene-based perovskite-silicon tandem solar panels, with plans to produce panels that define the state of the art. The first graphene-based solar farm is being established this year. Emmanuel Kymakis, a co-author, noted that graphene has become the most intriguing material in solar energy research due to its versatility and conductivity.

The application of graphene to solar energy generation was recognized as a priority since the start of the Graphene Flagship. These new results underpin the following three years of work. The initiative strongly aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, demonstrating how advanced materials research can contribute to a cleaner, more sustainable energy future.

reading.title: Influencers: The Modern Entrepreneur
reading.passage:
Social media influencers have redefined modern marketing and entrepreneurship. By leveraging digital platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok, influencers construct unique personal brands that resonate with specific target audiences. They are skilled at connecting with online audiences, shaping follower behavior, and persuading people to purchase products. While early social media personalities primarily focused on content creation and audience engagement, modern influencers increasingly operate as full-scale entrepreneurs.

Entrepreneurs are people who identify opportunities, take on the risks of a business, and organize resources to establish ventures. Influencers who start their own product lines, apparel brands, or digital services certainly fall under this definition of entrepreneurship. Their established follower base provides a built-in customer network, significantly lowering traditional customer acquisition costs.

Unlike traditional business startups that require substantial initial capital, many influencer-led businesses begin with minimal overhead costs. An influencer's primary assets — their creativity, their audience, and their personal brand — are largely intangible. This makes the barrier to entry remarkably low compared to conventional entrepreneurship.

However, influencer businesses face unique challenges. Building and maintaining audience trust is essential, as a single controversy can destroy years of brand building. Influencers must constantly produce fresh, engaging content while simultaneously managing the operational side of their business ventures.

Not all social media influencers are categorized as entrepreneurs. Only those who launch their own commercial ventures — taking on financial risk and creating products or services — truly qualify. The rest, while influential, are better described as content creators or brand ambassadors rather than entrepreneurs in the traditional sense.

grammar.question: Such energy storage systems could deliver full electric power about 80 percent of the time, which is comparable to the performance of conventional power plants, the researchers says.

grammar.question: Eating most at breakfast instead of dinner could prevent obesity and high blood sugar.

grammar.question: Many newer disciplines have emerged from Biochemistry such as Enzymology, Endocrinology, Clinical Biochemistry, and Molecular Biochemistry. In contrast with these branches, certain specialties such as Agricultural Biochemistry and Pharmacological Biochemistry have also come up.

grammar.question: Big dogs are often mismatched from weak seniors because an elderly dog owner said old people need dogs.

grammar.question: The second and most complex step of extract the actual kaon decay amplitudes was performed at the National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center (NERSC), a DOE Office of Science user facility at DOE's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

grammar.question: Teachers' unions will be obliged to protects teacher rights such as setting standards on how long a teacher can work and what duties they may undertake.

grammar.question: Exactly a year on from the discovery that a cheap steroid drug prevented Covid deaths, researchers say they have found other life-saving therapy.

grammar.question: Hence in the earlier book, Plato advocates an open and strict censorship of poetry, introduced certain charges hitherto unelaborated.

grammar.question: Parents should not assume that all cartoons are acceptable and appropriate because little contain violence.

grammar.question: When Kornberg was a medical student, he _____ a research indicating that high levels of bilirubin frequently occurred as a result of a reduced capacity to excrete it.

grammar.question: The analytical method Aristotle used is not _______ to a literary study and is sometimes too artificial or formula-prone in its conclusions.

grammar.question: Mario Bross _____ turtles like he always did, though better than ever thanks to new technology of Nintendo Switch.

grammar.question: Green plants depend on only four simple inputs—carbon dioxide, water, mineral salts, and sunlight—for their entire growth process, a requirement that stands in contrast from the nutritional needs of animals.
